sec: Etiology of acquired hypopituitarism, TSH and ACTH deficits

items.q: Match the cause of acquired hypopituitarism to its epidemiological frequency ranking — 1) Stalk effect 2) Sheehan's syndrome 3) Viper bite 4) Secondary empty sella syndrome … A) Most common cause (1st) B) Second most common cause (2nd) C) Third most common cause (3rd) D) Fourth most common cause (4th)
items.exp: Stalk effect is 1st m/c, Sheehan's is 2nd, viper bite envenomation is 3rd, and 2° empty sella is 4th. (Book p952)

items.q: Which infectious or infiltrative entity is NOT listed among the causes of acquired hypopituitarism?
items.exp: Causes include TB, histoplasmosis, HIV, toxoplasmosis, sarcoidosis, and LCH; Whipple disease is not listed. (Book p952)

items.q: Cranial radiation exposure exceeding what cumulative absorbed dose threshold is recognized to cause hypopituitarism?
items.exp: Cranial radiation exceeding 18 Gy is a recognized cause of hypopituitarism. (Book p952)

items.q: Which anterior pituitary hormone deficiency is clinically the least prominent in acquired hypopituitarism?
items.exp: TSH deficiency is the least prominent because 20% of thyroid hormone synthesis occurs autonomously without TSH. (Book p952)

items.q: In hypopituitarism, the most clinically prominent and life-threatening anterior pituitary hormone deficiency is ___.
items.exp: ACTH deficiency is the most prominent and critical deficit in hypopituitarism. (Book p952)

items.q: A 36-year-old agricultural laborer is bitten by a Russell viper. Two months later, he presents with profound fatigue, asthenia, and postural hypotension. What ranked cause of acquired hypopituitarism does this represent?
items.exp: Viper bite is the third most common cause of acquired hypopituitarism. (Book p952)

items.q: Assess the characteristics of corticotroph cells in hypopituitarism: I Corticotrophs are located in the central portion of the anterior pituitary gland. II Rapidly developing hypopituitarism is typically characterized by acute cortisol insufficiency.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Corticotrophs are centrally located, induced by stress, and rapid hypopituitarism is dominated by cortisol insufficiency. (Book p952)

items.q: Why do patients with secondary adrenal insufficiency from ACTH deficiency NOT exhibit hyperkalemia or severe salt wasting?
opts: Aldosterone secretion is preserved via the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system
Cortisol deficiency directly promotes distal tubular potassium excretion
Pituitary vasopressin compensates for loss of renal mineralocorticoid actions
Adrenal medullary catecholamines stimulate collecting duct sodium reabsorption
items.exp: Secondary adrenal insufficiency lacks aldosterone deficiency because the RAS axis maintains aldosterone synthesis. (Book p952)

items.q: In ACTH deficiency, serum cortisol is inversely proportional to circulating ___ counts, resulting in relative peripheral eosinophilia.
items.exp: Cortisol is inversely proportional to eosinophils; hypocortisolemia therefore manifests with eosinophilia. (Book p952)

items.q: Match the adrenal deficiency state to its hallmark clinical findings — 1) ACTH deficiency (Secondary) 2) Aldosterone deficiency (Primary RAS deficiency) … A) Postural hypotension, hypoglycemia, hyponatremia with NO hyperpigmentation or hyperkalemia B) Salt craving, dehydration, and hyperkalemia
items.exp: ACTH deficiency causes hypotension, hypoglycemia, and hyponatremia without aldosterone deficits; aldosterone lack causes salt craving, dehydration, and hyperkalemia. (Book p952)

items.q: Which feature is NOT typically seen in isolated secondary ACTH deficiency?
items.exp: Hyperpigmentation requires elevated ACTH/MSH and occurs in Addison disease, not in pituitary ACTH deficiency. (Book p952)

items.q: What proportion of endogenous thyroid hormone is synthesized by the thyroid gland independent of pituitary TSH stimulation?
items.exp: 20% of thyroid hormone is produced autonomously by the gland itself. (Book p952)
